item.title: Subsurface marine heat surge produces delayed climate impacts in the North Pacific
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 20 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04223-2

Subsurface marine heatwaves in the eastern North Pacific transported significant heat and volume anomalies into the tropics during multi-year, trans-basin migrations, according to analyses of Argo profile and ocean reanalysis data.
item.dc:title: Subsurface marine heat surge produces delayed climate impacts in the North Pacific

Yu Zhang

item.title: Dietary shifts during food stress in southern Madagascar informed by satellite remote sensing
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 20 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04162-y

Satellite-derived vegetation conditions track primary shifts from staple or aid-supported foods to less-preferred fallback foods during food stress, and only weakly track standard food-security indices, based on monthly dietary surveys of 602 households in southern Madagascar since 2018.
item.dc:title: Dietary shifts during food stress in southern Madagascar informed by satellite remote sensing
item.dc:creator: Alexandria N. Berry
Christopher D. Golden
Joanna B. Upton
Angela J. Rigden
Peter J. Huybers

item.title: Long-term limits on maximum ice sheet thickness around central Antarctic Peninsula nunataks
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 20 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04202-7

Nuclide ratios indicate that Antarctic Peninsula Ice Sheet surfaces of more than 121 – 170 m above current ice levels at Mount Faith, Mount Sullivan, and Engel Peaks have been ice-free for millions of years contrasting with models which predict <250 m of thinning since the Last Glacial Maximum, suggesting overestimation of sea-level contribution from the central and eastern Peninsula
item.dc:title: Long-term limits on maximum ice sheet thickness around central Antarctic Peninsula nunataks
